Hi Soojin,

We're at the final sign stage internally and procurement raised one last ask: can Redwood include explicit language around reserved GPU queueing behavior for our reserved pool? Specifically, we need assurance that during our defined peak windows (US business hours) requests for the reserved SKU won't be queued behind host-level batch jobs for more than 200ms p95 per token, and that there is a service-level headroom for priority lanes when we spike.

I've attached the draft SLA your AE shared earlier for context. Legal/procurement want either (A) a quantified carveout in the Dedicated addendum or (B) a runbook/commitment plus credits calculation if that SLO is missed.

Can Redwood support either approach? If so, what would the workable numbers be (headroom %, credits formula) and how would you operationalize monitoring?

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the draft. Short answer: yes, we can support a measured carveout and attach a runbook plus an SLA amendment. Two quick options that are commonly acceptable:

1) Contract amendment that defines a "priority-lane reservation" for up to 15% of the pool during defined peak windows (Mon-Fri 8am-6pm PT). When active this reservation prevents non-priority work from preempting your requests; measured p95 per-token tail latencies for priority lanes must remain under 250ms. Failure to meet that SLO triggers credits as defined below.

2) Operational runbook + monitoring: we expose the queue occupancy and priority-lane utilization metrics to a shared dashboard, and we agree on a headroom commitment (e.g., 15% baseline + an additional 10% on 30min moving avg traffic spikes). If the moving avg exceeds threshold for >10min and p95 exceeds threshold, we execute an escalation and apply credits.

For both we propose this credits formula (example): 5% of monthly Dedicated fee for each SLA breach window (up to a cap of 50% monthly credits).

I'm attaching a diagram that maps queue states to policy actions and a first-pass amendment that encodes the priority-lane behavior. If you can share the expected QPS distribution and typical inference size (tokens per call) for your peak and baseline hours that would help us tighten numbers.

Proposed next step: 30-min call with Ben (SLA/product ops) and David (runtime) to walk the runbook and monitoring. Are you available tomorrow?

Warmly,

Alex / team —

Thanks for looping procurement & legal. Per your ask on retention: Redwood retains per-request latency traces and anonymized KV-cache fingerprints for 90 days by default on Dedicated; for enterprise addenda we can extend to 365 days with an encrypted archival option (customer-managed KMS) if you need forensic access. We'll add that as a clause in the amendment.

On the technical numbers, David pulled some runtime runs and we propose the following (this is conservative but field-tested):

- Priority-lane reservation: 12% of pool capacity reserved for SentinelCap during peak windows (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 PT).
- Headroom scaling: automated additive burst allowance of +8% when 5-min moving avg > 80% of reserved lane for >5 minutes (capped at +20% total).
- Latency SLO: p95 per-token for priority lane <= 230ms; p99 <= 520ms (p99 is advisory and tied to credits only if > 600ms).
- Credits: 4% monthly fee per qualifying breach window (30 min window), stackable up to 40%/month.

Operationally we will:
- Expose a dedicated dashboard with: priority-lane occupancy, queue depth histogram, p50/p95/p99 per-token latency, and retention export.
- Auto-alert to SentinelCap and Redwood SRE if priority-lane p95 exceeds 230ms for >10 minutes.
- Run a joint post-incident review with remediation timeline.

I've attached SLA_amendment_v2 that encodes the above and a redlined section for the retention clause. If those numbers look acceptable we'll route to Legal for minor wording changes.

Soojin (I'll wait to book Ben/David and Lauren into your 11am slot — can you confirm?)

Alex / all —

Thanks for the discussion yesterday. After product + ops review we've agreed to approve a limited carveout under these binding conditions (finals to be captured in the Dedicated Addendum):

1) Priority lane reservation of 12% during agreed peak windows (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 PT).
2) Headroom additive bursts up to +8% automatically, with manual escalation for >15% bursts for >30 minutes.
3) SLO: p95 per-token <= 230ms for priority lane. If p95 > 230ms for a 30-minute window, SentinelCap receives 4% of monthly Dedicated fee as credit for that window. Credits stack for multiple windows up to a 40% monthly cap.
4) Data retention: standard 90 days; SentinelCap may opt-in for 365-day encrypted archival; costs for extended storage will be billed as a pass-through.
5) Redwood requires a read-only dashboard role for SentinelCap with the queueing metrics and an agreed escalation contact list.
6) This carveout is limited to the first 12 months post-activation; after 12 months both parties will review utilization and may re-negotiate headroom percentages.

Two operational caveats: our runtime can give near-real-time queue histograms but we cannot guarantee absolute zero queuing for non-priority tenants in certain emergency maintenance scenarios — those are handled under our maintenance SLA and excluded from credits except during unscheduled incidents caused by Redwood. We'll add firm language in the exclusions section.

If procurement/legal are good with the wording I can route the redline to Legal for signature and draft the DocuSign envelope.
